t: You're looking at the sculpture of Sylvia Pankhurst in Mile End Park, in Bethnal Green. It honours a leading English suffragette and socialist. She was the youngest daughter of two founders of the Independent Labour Party, and with her mother and sister she formed the Women's Social and Political Union at their home. She then worked to organise working-class women in London's East End, which is why a memorial to her stands in this part of the city. In nineteen fourteen she broke with her mother and sister's leadership over a wartime political truce.
